items.prompt_middleenglish: Whan that Aprill with his shoures soote / The droghte of March hath perced to the roote, / And bathed every veyne in swich licour / Of which vertu engendred is the flour.
items.prompt_en: Translate. (General Prologue to Canterbury Tales, lines 1-4)
reference: When April with his sweet showers has pierced the drought of March to the root, and bathed every vein in such liquid from which power the flower is engendered.
When April with his sweet showers has penetrated March's drought to the root, and bathed every vein in such moisture by whose power the flower is generated.
When April's sweet showers have pierced the drought of March to the root and bathed every vein in such liquid whose virtue produces the flower.

items.prompt_middleenglish: A knyght ther was, and that a worthy man, / That fro the tyme that he first bigan / To riden out, he loved chivalrye, / Trouthe and honour, fredom and curteisye.
reference: There was a knight, and that a worthy man, who from the time that he first began to ride out, loved chivalry, truth and honor, generosity and courtesy.
A knight there was, and that a distinguished man, who from the time he first began to go on campaigns, loved chivalry, integrity and honor, nobility and courtesy.
There was a knight, a worthy man, who from the time he first began to ride forth loved chivalry, fidelity and honor, generosity and courtliness.

items.prompt_middleenglish: Ther hales in at the halle dor an aghlich mayster, / On the most on the molde on mesure hyghe.
items.prompt_en: Translate. (Sir Gawain and the Green Knight, lines 136-137)
reference: There hastens in at the hall door a terrible master, among the biggest on earth in height measure.
There comes rushing in at the hall door a fearsome lord, one of the tallest men on earth in measured height.
There hurries in at the hall door an awesome master, the largest on earth in stature.

items.prompt_middleenglish: I craue in this court a Crystemas gomen, / For hit is Yol and Nwe Yer, and here ar yep mony.
reference: I crave in this court a Christmas game, for it is Yule and New Year, and here are many vigorous men.
I request in this court a Christmas sport, for it is Christmas and New Year, and here are many active folk.
I ask in this court for a Christmas entertainment, for it is the season and here are many spirited men.
